rating_explained: The CNN piece reports Trump publicly rejected Iran's proposal on Sept 26, calling it 'unacceptable,' after Iran offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within a week and resume nuclear talks in exchange for the U.S. lifting its naval blockade and waiving oil sanctions. USA Today independently confirms Trump's 'that deal would not be acceptable' remark to reporters on Sept 26 and cites the Wall Street Journal's Sept 25 reporting that the denied proposal included opening Hormuz, resuming nuclear talks, and lifting the U.S. blockade of Iranian ports. The New York Post, also citing the WSJ, confirms the reported remark that Trump 'told aides he expects to resume bombing the country after the midterm elections,' and confirms the deal would have restarted nuclear talks in exchange for lifting the blockade. On the Iranian side, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told CNN that no formal rejection had come through mediator channels: 'nothing has been conveyed to us from the mediators yet.' The only element I could not verify firsthand is the WSJ's own wording on the bombing remark, since the Journal is paywalled; it reaches me secondhand via the Post's direct attribution. Every other checkable element of the claim matches named, published reporting, so the verdict is accurate.

The same analysis documents the ledger's Biden-era entries: the Small Business Administration's $22.2 billion in flagged fraudulent loans was actually identified during the Biden administration, and a 'top ten' enforcement entry touting four captured fugitives includes three charged in 2019 and 2024, before this administration took office. Even the administration-friendly WLT Report confirms the shifting headline numbers — Vance's Sept 25 update claims $260.7B 'uncovered' since January 2025, $72B stopped and $58.9B recovered — and concedes 'uncovered' means estimated suspicious payments flagged for examination, not court judgments, which matches the NYT's language about unverifiable or prematurely counted allegations quoted by PoliticalWire. One caveat: the NYT piece itself is paywalled, so I verified its content through published excerpts plus independent corroboration. Because the claim accurately describes the NYT's findings and those findings are independently substantiated, the verdict is accurate.

Memeorandum's aggregator page lists it as 'Trump allies could use midterms counting window to disrupt results, experts warn (George Chidi/The Guardian),' and PoliticalWire's own Sept 27 coverage links directly to theguardian.com, confirming the original Guardian piece exists with this headline and author; the original Guardian URL was not directly fetchable in this environment. I opened the provided mirror (thebullpost.press) and found its text consistent with the attributed Guardian piece, including the direct quotes, so the mirror URL is retained as a confirmed verbatim carrier. The substance checks out: the piece quotes former deputy homeland security adviser Caitlin Durkovich telling a Brennan Center for Justice briefing that the administration could 'use the claim of foreign interference at the end of voting days to either seize equipment or to seize ballots, whether they're legally justified to do so or not,' quotes Brennan Center's Larry Norden ('This is the biggest threat right now') and former EAC chair Ben Hovland (on the administration's 'narrative of fraud' and 'live ballots'). This is a warnings story, and the claim's 'could' framing is its honest frame: the experts are predicting future risk, not asserting past facts, and it is accurate that they issued these warnings.

rating_explained: The arrest record is established: Brian Cole Jr. was arrested Dec 4, 2025, and on July 7, 2026 Judge Amir Ali denied his motion to dismiss, ruling Trump's Jan 6 pardons do not cover him because he 'had not been convicted of the conduct at issue when the President issued the pardon' and was not charged until nearly a year after the proclamation (WSYR/iHeart court coverage). Bondi did make the 'languished' remark — 'This case languished. It sat there for four years collecting dust' — but on Fox & Friends on Dec 5, 2025, not this weekend; it is being re-amplified now alongside Tucker Carlson's Sept 17, 2026 interview of Cole's parents, who say their son was framed (confirmed by WLT Report quoting Carlson's X post). The factual core of Bondi's claim comes from Deputy FBI Director Dan Bongino himself: a fresh team assigned about two months before the arrest 'scoured existing evidence,' and the key evidence — credit-card purchases of bomb components, cell-phone and vehicle activity from Jan 5 — was 'gathered under the previous administration' (RealClearInvestigations, citing AP). But the blanket claim of four years of inaction is contradicted by the on-the-record record: former director Wray testified under oath the FBI was 'aggressively investigating' with a dedicated team, and the FBI made repeated public appeals and doubled its reward — though a January 2025 House GOP report alleged resources were diverted as early as February 2021. So the arrest is real and the evidence-predated-the-new-team claim is supported by the FBI's own deputy director, but 'no one did anything for four years' is an unverifiable characterization with named contradictory evidence on the record — hence mixed. The pardon fight is also real: the motion was denied, trial is set for February 2027.

rating_explained: The Washington Examiner quotes Trump's Saturday-night announcement verbatim: he approved new fuel-economy standards that 'TERMINATE' Biden's 'ridiculous EV Mandate,' said the old rules 'cost our Great Auto Manufacturers $Billions,' promised 'LOWER PRICES, saving families thousands,' and declared 'Plants are coming back, and Jobs are returning, to Michigan, Ohio, Indiana, South Carolina,' with Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy confirming the rule lands Monday. Reuters (via LA Post, Sept 26) independently confirms the underlying action: DOT will finalize sharply lower fuel-economy standards through 2031 on Monday, reversing Biden's push, with Trump saying they will lower new-vehicle prices; the department's proposal sets a 34.5 mpg fleet average by 2031 versus 50.4 mpg under Biden, and DOT's own estimate says the change cuts per-vehicle costs by $930. The NYT (via memeorandum) similarly reports the administration will 'move on Monday to sharply scale back fuel-efficiency rules,' killing a federal effort to speed EV adoption. Two caveats: lower prices and returning jobs are Trump's forward-looking claims, not established outcomes — DOT's own figures project roughly $185 billion more in fuel spending and ~100 billion extra gallons consumed through 2050 — and the Examiner's '2024 standards set by Biden's EPA' slightly conflates EPA emissions rules with NHTSA fuel-economy standards. The claim faithfully describes the announcement, so the verdict is accurate.
